name: אינטגרל מסוים בשברים חלקיים – גורם חוזר (x+9)² מ-(−1) עד 1 (באנגלית)
questiontext:
By expressing the integrand as the sum of its partial fractions, find the following definite integral:

\[ \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}. \]

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Find an antiderivative \(F\) of the integrand with partial fractions (decomposition, coefficients, term-by-term integration), then evaluate \(F\) at the limits.
Step 1 — The form of the decomposition
In order to calculate

\[ \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} \]

we need to express

\[ {{CT:2}} \]

as the sum of its partial fractions. The denominator is a repeated linear factor:
Partial fractions: \( \frac{p(x)}{(x-a)(x-b)}=\frac{A}{x-a}+\frac{B}{x-b} \); a repeated factor \( (x-a)^2 \) gives \( \frac{A}{x-a}+\frac{B}{(x-a)^2} \); an irreducible \( x^2+bx+c \) gives \( \frac{Ax+B}{x^2+bx+c} \)

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:2}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:4}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}}{{CT:6}} + {{CT:7}}{{CT:8}} \end{array} \]

Step 2 — Finding the coefficients
Multiplying both sides by \({{CT:9}}\) gives

\[ {{CT:10}} = A\left({{CT:11}}\right)+B \]

Substituting \({{CT:3}}={{CT:12}}\) makes the \(A\) term vanish, and comparing the coefficients of \({{CT:3}}\) on both sides gives \(A\):

\[ B={{CT:13}},\qquad A={{CT:14}} \]

Hence

\[ {{CT:2}} = {{CT:15}}, \]

Step 3 — An antiderivative
Integrating term by term,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int {{CT:15}} d{{CT:3}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:16}} \int {{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}} + {{CT:17}} \int {{CT:8}} d{{CT:3}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:18}} + {{CT:19}} +c \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:20}} +c \end{array} \]

Step 4 — Substituting the limits
We need

\[ \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} \]

so, recall that if

\[ \int f(x) dx = F(x) \]

then

\[ \int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b). \]

Thus, define

\[ F({{CT:3}}) = {{CT:21}} \]

Then,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:22}} - \left[{{CT:23}}\right] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:24}} \end{array} \]
